title: Quantization error propagation through layers
hook: Round every layer's weights and measure what reaches the end: with depth it grows more like a square root than an avalanche, until layers start to amplify.

verified.claim: For a linear layer the output error is exactly the weight error times the input.
In this stack, error at depth 16 was about 3.5 times the error at depth 1 at gains up to 2, and much larger at gain 4.
QUANTIZATION.md says calibration is needed to choose fixed activation scales, not for formats with dynamic activation scaling, and that biases stay floating point.
A checkpoint can mix formats and plain float layers per module.
Formats the device lacks fall back to dequantizing for the multiply, and a test covers this for int8.
The GPTQ abstract reports quantizing to 3 or 4 bits with little accuracy loss on large language models.

unchecked: The stack is a toy: random matrices, tanh, no attention. Real diffusion models have other structure, and we did not measure one.
The gain setting is approximate: a random matrix's largest singular value is near the value named, not exactly on it.
Which layers matter most in any real model, including the common advice about first and last layers, which we did not test.
